teams.heading: Fiji defeat Canada to secure Pacific Nations Cup final place against Japan
teams.body: The defending champions secured their place in the Pacific Nations Cup final against Japan after defeating Canada in Osaka. Before the match, Canada head coach Stephen Meehan noted that many of Fiji's top players were absent due to professional club commitments, but warned his side of the "free-spirited challenge" posed by the Flying Fijians' physical and expansive play. Fiji's victory sets up a Tokyo final as they look to defend their crown.

lead.why: Fiji's qualification for the Pacific Nations Cup final after defeating Canada is the day's primary sporting achievement.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs accuses RFU of having 'blinkers on' over Steve Borthwick backing
teams.body: Ben Youngs has criticised RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney and performance director Conor O’Shea for their "blinkers on" approach in awarding Steve Borthwick a contract extension. Despite what O’Shea termed a "horrendous" 2026 Six Nations campaign—where England finished with just one win—the board have extended Borthwick’s terms until after the 2028 championship. Youngs questioned the accountability of the RFU hierarchy on the For The Love Of Rugby podcast, suggesting both Sweeney and O’Shea must also depart if Borthwick fails at next year's World Cup.

lead.why: High-profile criticism from a legendary former player regarding the head coach's job security and RFU accountability is the day's most significant talking point.

teams.heading: IRFU rules out staging upcoming Six Nations matches in America
teams.body: The IRFU has confirmed there are “currently no plans or discussions” regarding the possibility of moving Six Nations fixtures to the United States. While World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin had previously highlighted the commercial potential of hosting an Ireland-Italy encounter stateside to engage expatriate fans, the Irish governing body dismissed the proposal. The IRFU reiterated its commitment to the traditional championship structure, maintaining that home fixtures remain a central part of the tournament's unique appeal to local supporters.

teams.heading: Rhea Clarke and Evie Gallagher start for Scotland against Canada
teams.body: Scrum-half Rhea Clarke makes her first start for Scotland in Saturday’s WXV Series opener against Canada at Hive Stadium. Evie Gallagher also returns to the starting line-up on the openside flank for her first international appearance since last year’s World Cup. Interim head coach Dave Butcher has named a side captained by Rachel Malcolm, with Helen Nelson providing leadership in the backs. The transition under Butcher has been described as "pretty seamless" by the players following the coaching staff changes.
